title: Refactor policy decision mesh + canonical schema validator for routing rules
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Overview: We are refactoring the routing policy engine so that rule evaluation is expressed as a canonical "decision mesh" IR and validated by a single, authoritative schema validator. The goal is to eliminate divergent validators across runtime, console, and private deployments, enable staged migration of legacy rule formats, and provide deterministic diagnostics and fix suggestions for authoring errors.

Scope: 1) Define a stable canonical schema (JSON Schema + typed constraints) for the decision-mesh IR representing region selection, tier routing, and fallback variants. 2) Implement a modular validator that performs syntactic and semantic checks (type checking, region/tier existence, variant compatibility, circular-fallback detection, probabilistic weights sum, and capacity-aware hints). 3) Provide a backward-compatibility adapter that transpiles legacy DSL/configs into the canonical IR with lint warnings. 4) Integrate the validator into the runtime ingestion path, the Console rule editor, and the private deployment CLI. 5) Add robust telemetry and structured error messages to aid rollouts and customer diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical schema document published and reviewed by PM/Design/Infra
Validator unit tests with >90% branch coverage and comprehensive property/fuzz tests
Backward adapter converts >=99% of customer rules without manual edits in dry-run tests
Console shows schema errors with actionable suggestions and exact AST locations
Runtime rejects invalid configs during deploy and exposes clear audit log entries
Canary rollout (10% of Dedicated clusters) running validator in enforce mode with automated rollback on regressions
tasks: Design canonical decision-mesh IR and constraints -> design doc: drive.google.com/drive/fake-doc-DecisionMesh
Prototype typed AST validator (Rust) with pluggable checks
Implement transpiler for legacy DSL v1->IR with linting output
Add integration hook in config ingestion service (ingest-validator) and feature flag for dry-run
Console: surface structured validation errors and quick-fix suggestions
Add e2e tests against sample corpora (region-heavy, tier-weighted, fallback-chains)
Create migration playbook + deprecation timeline for customers
Instrument telemetry: validation_error_code, rule_hash, deployment_id, dry_run_flag
risks: High customer config heterogeneity - adapter may miss edge-case constructs
False positives from strict semantic checks could block existing deployments if enforcement flipped prematurely
Performance impact on ingestion path if validator is synchronous without caching
Mismatch between Console and runtime error semantics during migration window
mitigations: Start with dry-run mode across all control planes to collect real-world rule shapes
Expose feature flag for enforcement and granular allowlists per customer
Implement incremental validation cache keyed by rule hash and last-validated schema version
Coordinate Console + Runtime release and keep old validator available behind a compatibility flag for 6 weeks
notes:
Design choices considered: 1) JSON Schema alone is insufficient for cross-field invariants (e.g. probabilities, capacity hints) so we add a typed constraint layer that runs after basic schema validation. 2) Rust validator chosen for runtime safety and to enable reuse in the private on-prem binary. 3) Provide canonical-to-legacy source maps to generate helpful console diagnostics.

Migration plan (high-level): Phase 1 (dry-run): run transpiler and validator in dry-run across hosted and Dedicated configs for 3 weeks; collect telemetry and top N failure modes. Phase 2 (soft-enforce): enable enforcement for non-customer-impacting checks (lint-only) and expose quick-fixes in Console. Phase 3 (enforce): flip enforcement for low-risk customers, keep compatibility shim for complex enterprise accounts for an additional 6 weeks.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: drive.google.com/drive/fake-doc-DecisionMesh, RFC: confluence.redwood.ai/routing/decision-mesh-rfc, prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1432
